title: Generation of Self-assembled Vascularized Human Skin Equivalents
protocol: Prepare rat tail collagen stock at 8 mg/mL.
Expand endothelial cells to a density sufficient for seeding.
Expand fibroblasts to a density sufficient for seeding.
Expand keratinocytes to a density necessary for the epidermal component generation on day 7 of culture.
Seed 7.5 x 10^5 endothelial cells per dermal component.
Seed 7.5 x 10^4 fibroblasts per dermal component.
Seed 1.7 x 10^5 keratinocytes for the epidermal component generation after day 7 of culture.
Perform all cell centrifugation at 300 x g for 5 min.
Prepare two 1.7 mL capped microcentrifuge tubes, one for the acellular support and one for the cellular dermis.
Add 100 µL of culture grade 10x Phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) to each tube.
Add 8.6 µL of 1 N NaOH to each tube.
Place capped tubes on wet ice to chill for at least 10 min.
Prepare 1000 and 250 µL positive displacement pipettes for use.
Set volumes for the prepared pipettes to 375 µL and 125 µL, respectively.
Setup a normal 1000 µL pipette for 516 µL.
Load pipette tips onto the pipettes.
Use sterile forceps to place three 12-well size culture inserts into a sterile 12-well tissue culture plate in the center columns.
Set out cold media appropriate for fibroblast and endothelial cell types.
Place one tube containing acellular support on a rack with contents visible.
Keep another tube containing cellular dermis on ice.
Remove 8 mg/mL collagen stock from refrigeration.
Place the removed collagen stock on wet ice.
Add 516 µL of media to a cold capped tube.
Immediately add 375 µL of cold collagen using a 1000 µL positive displacement pipette.
Dispense the collagen into the solution (not to the side of the tube).
Switch to a prepared 250 µL positive displacement pipette and mix quickly but gently to prevent bubble formation, without removing the tip from the solution.
Mix until the solution is homogeneous in color, typically taking about 5 pipette cycles or 10 seconds.
Draw from different positions of the tube (bottom and top) for uniform mixing.
Disperse 125 µL of acellular collagen onto the membrane of each of the three 12-well culture inserts immediately after mixing.
Rock the dish to ensure uniform coverage of the acellular collagen gel.
If rocking does not create uniform coverage, use a pipette tip to gently spread the collagen around the membrane without applying pressure.
Trypsinize and count the endothelial and fibroblast cell lines.
Suspend 7.5 x 10^5 endothelial cells in 258 μL of their respective media.
Suspend 7.5 x 10^4 fibroblasts in 258 μL of their respective media.
Combine the endothelial and fibroblast cell suspensions to create a 516 µL aliquot.
Maintain the combined cell suspension on wet ice until use.
Prepare 1000 and 250 μL positive displacement pipettes for use.
Set volumes (375 μL and 250 μL, respectively) in advance of later steps.
Setup a normal 1000 µL pipette for dispensing 516 µL.
Remove the 12 well plate of acellular collagen from the incubator.
Check if the collagen has gelled after 30 minutes; proceed only if it has successfully gelled.
Remove the 1.7 mL capped tube containing 10x PBS and NaOH from wet ice.
Loosen all caps on cell suspension and cold capped tube.
Place the stock collagen (8 mg/mL) on wet ice with the cap open.
Add 516 µL of cooled cell suspension to the cold capped tube.
Pipette 375 µL of cold collagen solution directly into the tube using a 1000 µL positive displacement pipette.
Expel all collagen from pipette into the tube and discard the tip.
Immediately switch to a 250 µL positive displacement pipette to mix the collagen solution.
Mix the collagen solution quickly but gently without forming bubbles, drawing from different positions in the tube (bottom and top) for uniform mixing.
Continue mixing until the solution is homogenous, about 5 pipette cycles or 10 seconds.
Transfer 250 µL of cellular collagen solution onto the acellular collagen supports in each of the three 12-well culture inserts.
Rock the dish and/or use a positive displacement pipette to gently move the freshly seeded cellular collagen around without disturbing the acellular layer.
Move the 12-well plate immediately to a 37 °C cell culture incubator for at least 30 minutes.
Tilt the plate after 30 minutes to assess gelation and ensure the collagen is solidified.
Add 500 µL of blend media to the upper chamber and 1000 µL to the lower chamber of the insert, adding slowly to the side of the well to prevent disruption of the collagen.
Ensure that the collagen gel is submerged by adding more media if necessary.
Place the well plate in the cell incubator for overnight incubation.
Change 10% FBS media in VHSE wells to 5% FBS half fibroblast, half endothelial media supplemented with 100 µg/mL L-Ascorbic Acid.
Add 500 µL of the new media to the upper chamber of the culture insert at the side of the well carefully.
Add 1000 µL of the new media to the lower chamber.
Renew media every 2 days (SD4 and SD6) until Submersion Day 7 (SD7).
Remove media from the wells using a manual pipette.
Make up fresh L-ascorbic acid stock at 100 mg/mL daily for use in the VHSE culture.
Prepare a new aliquot of media each feeding day, adding freshly prepared L-Ascorbic Acid to maintain its effectiveness.
Seed keratinocytes to establish the epidermis on SD7.
Shorten submersion period to 5 days and seed epidermis on SD5 if contraction occurs before SD7.
Culture keratinocytes to their confluency limit before trypsinization and seeding onto VHSEs.
Trypsinize keratinocytes when they reach the appropriate confluence (30% for N/TERT-1 cells, 75-80% for other cell lines).
Count and suspend 510,000 cells in 600 µL of Human Skin Equivalent Differentiation media supplemented with 5% FBS.
Seed 200 μL of the suspension per construct to allow 170,000 cells/construct.
Using a manual pipette, collect and discard media currently in the bottom chamber for each construct well.
Collect as much media as possible, including any stuck under the permeable membrane by gently placing the pipette tip under the culture insert membrane.
Discard media from the top chamber similarly.
Add 1 mL of HSE media supplemented with 5% FBS to the lower chamber of each well.
Add 200 µL of cell suspension to the top chamber of each well, seeding directly onto the dermal construct surface.
Let keratinocytes settle for 2 h in the incubator.
Two hours after seeding the keratinocytes, carefully add 300 µL of HSE media supplemented with 5% FBS to the top chamber of each construct well.
Slowly pipette media onto the side of the culture insert without disturbing settled keratinocytes.
Remove media from both the upper and lower chambers with a manual pipettor on Submersion Day 8/9 (SD8 or SD9).
Make up HSE media supplemented with 1% FBS and 100 µg/mL L-ascorbic acid.
Add 500 μL media into the top chamber.
Add 1 mL media into the bottom chamber.
Make up serum-free HSE differentiation media with 100 μg/mL L-ascorbic acid.
Remove media from both upper and lower chambers using a manual pipettor.
Load 500 μL into the upper chamber.
Load 1 mL into the lower chamber.
Tilt the plate to collect media waste from the upper chamber without touching the epidermal layer.
Add approximately 2 mL of sterile water to surrounding wells to maintain humidity.
Check the plate a few hours later to ensure keratinocytes are at air-liquid interface.
Remove any remaining media in the upper chamber if present.
Adjust media levels in VHSEs as needed for air lift culture.
Remove any media from the top chamber of VHSEs on ALI Day 2.
Calculate the volume of media needed using the recorded amount previously removed.
Add calculated volume of serum-free HSE media supplemented with L-ascorbic acid to the bottom chamber.
Place the plate back into the cell incubator after media addition.
Keep track of the volume used per day for routine maintenance.
Renew media of the lower chamber every 2-3 days using serum-free HSE media with 100 µg/mL L-ascorbic acid.
Adjust and track the media level needed in the bottom chamber for air-liquid interface (ALI).
Check and adjust the media level daily until consistent ALI levels are established to maintain a hydrated epidermal layer without pooled media.
Remove all media from the upper and lower chambers of each well.
Add 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS (pH 6.9) to the upper chamber wall, avoiding direct contact with the construct.
Add 1 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde solution to the lower chamber.
Expose constructs for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Remove 4% paraformaldehyde solution after 5 minutes.
Add 0.5% Triton X-100 in 4% paraformaldehyde solution to both chambers as previously described.
Expose constructs for 1 hour at room temperature.
Carefully remove the permeabilization/fixation solution from both chambers.
Wash samples three times with 1x PBS.
Wrap the dish in plastic wrap followed by foil and store at 4°C or proceed immediately to staining.
Turn an insert upside down and place it over its well on the well plate.
Stabilize the insert with one hand while cutting about half of the circumference of the insert membrane as close to the plastic housing as possible using fine tip forceps or a precision knife.
Use fine tip forceps to grab the edge of the cut membrane flap and gently peel off the porous membrane along with the VHSE construct.
If the VHSE construct separates easily, it should fall into the well below. If stuck, use fine tip forceps or a small scoopula to move it to the well carefully.
Dip in PBS if necessary to prevent the VHSEs from drying out during the process.
Discard any remaining pieces of the insert membrane.
Keep the culture insert housing in each well to hold the VHSEs in a submerged position during staining.
Prepare primary antibody stains in 700 µL of blocking buffer per construct well.
Remove PBS from the well using a manual pipette carefully, avoiding aspiration from the VHSEs.
Add the primary stain solution to each well.
Place the culture insert housing into the well to keep the VHSE submerged.
Wrap the well plate with plastic wrap.
Stain for 48 hours in 4 °C refrigeration without agitation.
After 48 hours, prepare secondary antibodies and chemical stains in 700 μL of blocking buffer per well.
Remove the culture insert housing and the primary stain solution.
Wash with 1x PBS three times for 5 minutes each.
Add the secondary stain solution to the well.
Place the culture insert housing back into the well to keep VHSE construct submerged.
Expose for 48 hours in a 4 °C refrigerator without agitation or rocking.
Remove the stain solution with a manual pipettor after 48 hours of exposure.
Wash three times gently with PBS, avoiding direct application onto the VHSEs.
Rehydrate with excess PBS and place the culture insert housing back into the well to keep VHSE submerged.
Wrap the storage container in plastic wrap and foil to minimize evaporation and light exposure.
Add 100% methanol to a small shallow glass container.
Remove the construct from the well plate using forceps/scoopula and place in the methanol filled container.
Add more methanol if necessary to ensure the construct is submerged.
Dehydrate the VHSE construct in methanol for 3 x 10 min immersions.
Fully replace methanol after each immersion.
Promptly remove methanol after the last bath.
Immediately after removing methanol, add methyl salicylate and submerge the VHSE in 5 x 5 min immersions.
Fully replace the reagent after each immersion.
Leave the VHSE in the 5th immersion solution for storage.
Image the construct or store at 4 °C.
Complete all imaging as soon as possible after clearing.
Check regularly to ensure sufficient methyl salicylate during extended storage.
Place a clean mixing vessel on a weighing balance and tare the scale.
Add 27 g of base component PDMS to the mixing vessel.
Add 3 g of crosslinker to achieve a total of 30 g PDMS mixture.
Stir the PDMS mixture vigorously for at least 4 min.
Pour the mixed PDMS into a 100-mm Petri dish or similar flat bottom heat resistant container.
De-gas the PDMS in a vacuum chamber until all bubbles disappear and PDMS becomes clear.
Release the vacuum slowly and remove the PDMS slowly.
Place the dish into an oven to cure overnight at 50-60 °C.
Cut out a circular well from the cured PDMS sheet using a steel punch or handheld precision knife.
Create a square patch around the circular well to form a single PDMS well.
Add a few drops of imaging solution into the PDMS well.
Check for leaks and repair with cyanoacrylate super glue if necessary.
Keep the imaging solution in the PDMS well when adding the VHSE.
Remove construct from 12-well plate using scoopula or fine tip forceps.
Place construct into the PDMS well onto the glass coverslip.
Position construct with the orientation of interest facing toward the objective.
For inverted microscope imaging, ensure epidermis is facing down.
For upright microscope imaging, face the epidermis up.
Transfer VHSE over the well plate if it falls.
Use a bent, flat tip scoopula for easy transfer.
Ensure the sample sits flat in the well with no folding.
Gently manipulate the sample with forceps or scoopula to straighten out if folded.
Add extra imaging solution temporarily to help straighten out the VHSE.
Fill the well with imaging solution to keep the sample hydrated.
Test for movement by tilting the PDMS well; if there is movement, remove some fluid drop wise until movement stops.
Place a glass slide over the well to minimize evaporation during imaging.
Check sample frequently during longer imaging sessions to ensure proper fluid levels.
If accessible, use a humidified chamber during imaging (optional).
Place the sample on the microscope stage and image through the glass coverslip window.
Regularly check hydration of the sample and add imaging solution as needed for continuous confocal imaging.
If sample is cleared with methyl salicylate, re-apply glue bonding periodically or transfer to new wells.
After imaging, float the sample with imaging fluid in the well.
Transfer the sample into its storage well using a scoopula or fine tip forceps.
Clean bottom glass before imaging, both inside and outside the well.
Check for leaks in PDMS wells and top glass coverslips before re-using, repair with glue as necessary.
Store samples as described in step 6.3.6.
Add PBS every few months to maintain stored samples.
If samples are cleared, store them in glass using methyl salicylate.
Check the levels of methyl salicylate regularly for cleared samples.
Image cleared samples as soon as possible due to rapid degradation.
